site.name: Volatility Farm
site.tagline: Independent short-term research on stocks in the days after they report earnings — what changed, what the market got right or wrong, and the risks over the next 10–30 days.

reports.dek: Q3 2026 sales rose only 1.5% to $5.14B, roughly in line with consensus, after the 25 August cyberattack cost ~300 bps of growth and ~$0.07 of EPS. Adjusted EPS was $0.73, below the company's own $0.80–0.82 guide. Q4 sales are now guided to fall 1–3%, and management expects 2027 to be "the trough", with electrophysiology and WATCHMAN still losing ground. The stock, already down 53% this year, traded ~8% lower at ~$41.64. Over the next 10–30 days the bad news is largely out; the question is whether a 14× multiple and insider buying can hold a floor before there is any growth to point to.
reports.headline: Boston Scientific called 2027 the trough and guided Q4 sales lower, but at 14× earnings with the CEO buying, the stock is priced for most of that bad news

reports.dek: Q3 2026 revenue rose 4% to $24.19B, slightly below the ~$24.37B consensus, and the core loss of $0.34 a share was wider than the ~$0.20 expected. Boeing will hold the 737 at 47 a month into 2027, move 52 a month to the second half of 2027, miss ~500 737 deliveries this year and guide 2027 free cash flow to ~$3B, against roughly $5.5B on the Street. The stock fell 10.7% to $168.18, a 52-week closing low. Over the next 10–30 days the question is whether oversold conditions bring a bounce or target cuts and a weak market-regime map extend the slide.
reports.headline: Boeing pushed its 737 ramp and its cash recovery out by a year, and a record backlog is not enough to stop the re-rating in the weeks after the reset

reports.dek: Q3 2026 adjusted net revenue rose 44% to a record $1.37B against a ~$1.26B consensus. Adjusted EPS was $0.18 against $0.17, and SoFi raised 2026 guidance and introduced a 2027 outlook of $6.4B revenue and $0.90 EPS. The stock came into the print at $14.46, down 45% year to date and 55% below its November 2025 high, and traded ~15% higher at ~$16.63 midday. But the Q4 guide is flat on Q3 revenue, and the 2027 plan assumes two rate hikes. Over the next 10–30 days the company has made its case; the FOMC on 28 Oct and the fintech peer prints decide whether a short-covering pop becomes a re-rating.
reports.headline: SoFi beat and raised from a 52-week low, but a 2.6-beta stock still needs the Fed and the fintech tape to keep the rally going

reports.dek: Fiscal Q1 2027 organic sales rose 4%, led by 2.4% volume growth, and core EPS of $2.00 beat the $1.88 consensus. P&G kept full-year guidance (core EPS ~$7.00, organic sales +1–3%) even as the commodity headwind grew to $1.4B from $1.0B. But core EPS rose only 1%, core gross margin fell 150 bps, and the stock ran from $145 to $159 in the two weeks before the print. Shares were ~3% higher pre-market at ~$162, above the $162 mean target. Over the next 10–30 days PG trades on its own and against the market; the Colgate, Clorox and Kimberly-Clark reads decide whether the staples rotation holds.
reports.headline: P&G's volumes are growing again and it held guidance through a bigger commodity hit, but the stock already rallied 10% into a quarter that barely grew earnings

reports.dek: Q3 2026 revenue rose 15% to $1.60B and adjusted EPS of $2.90 crushed the $1.85 consensus, with Magic: The Gathering up 34% to over $600M and Wizards earning a 49% margin. Hasbro raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1.575–1.625B, above the $1.48B consensus, and doubled its buyback target. But ~$55M of one-off tariff refunds helped, and the full-year revenue guide implies Q4 sales down 4–10%. Shares were ~2% higher pre-market at ~$100.5, after rising 12.5% in a month. Over the next 10–30 days HAS trades on its own news, and the Mattel and holiday-season reads decide whether it reaches its $107 high.
reports.headline: Magic made Hasbro's quarter and lifted the year, but the raised guide still implies a smaller Q4 and the stock ran 12% into the print

reports.dek: Q3 2026 EBIT-adjusted rose 22% to $4.1B (8.2% margin) and North America earned an 8.7% margin, with adjusted EPS of $3.70 just ahead of $3.63. GM also raised free-cash-flow guidance by $1.5B and authorised a new $20B buyback. But the full-year profit midpoint stayed at $15B and the EPS midpoint ($13.25) sits below the $13.48 consensus; International, China and GM Financial all fell, and US share slipped to 16.1%. Shares were ~8% lower pre-market at ~$76. Over the next 10–30 days GM trades with the market and the auto group; the buyback pace, Ford's print and the rate path decide whether the gap fills.
reports.headline: GM's trucks carried the quarter and a $20B buyback dwarfs the risk, but a capped profit guide sent the stock 8% lower

reports.dek: Q3 2026 core EPS of $9.18 beat the $7.43 consensus on an 86.8 combined ratio, $234M of favourable reserve development and record investment income, and Travelers bought back $1.5B of stock. But net written premiums were flat (+2% excluding the Canada sale), Business Insurance renewal premium change slowed to 4.1% and personal auto premiums fell 8%. The shares dropped ~5% pre-market and then recovered to ~$386 after the call. Over the next 10–30 days TRV trades with the commercial P&C group and against the market; Chubb, Hartford and Allstate's prints decide whether pricing worries or earnings power win.
reports.headline: Travelers beat by 24% and the market bought the dip, but a flat top line and decelerating commercial pricing leave the stock above its targets

reports.dek: Q3 2026 revenue rose 4% to $4.84B (+5% in constant currency) and adjusted EPS of $1.01 matched consensus. But gross margin fell 70 bps to 15.9%, Q4 EPS guidance of $1.03–1.13 sits below the $1.10 consensus, free cash flow was negative and the board named a new CEO from 1 January. Shares were ~19% lower pre-market at ~$42, after doubling between February and August. Over the next 10–30 days the company, not the market, decides the price; analyst resets and the Randstad, Adecco and Kelly prints show whether the gap extends toward $39 or starts to fill.
reports.headline: ManpowerGroup delivered the quarter it promised, but shrinking gross margin and a soft Q4 guide end a rally that had already doubled the stock

reports.dek: Q3 2026 combined ratio was 88.7 (89.5 a year ago) and EPS of $4.37 was about $4.60 before $170M of realised investment losses, above the $4.41 consensus. But net premiums written grew only 4% in the quarter and 2% in September, policies in force growth slowed to 6%, and a $1.3B unrealised bond loss in September cut book value growth. The shares fell ~2.6% pre-market to ~$217, after a 7.5% rally into the print. Over the next 10–30 days PGR trades with the P&C insurers and against the market; the 3 November conference call and Allstate's results decide whether growth fears or underwriting quality win.
reports.headline: Progressive's underwriting is still the best in the industry, but 2% September premium growth confirms the slowdown the stock now has to price

reports.dek: Q3 2026 sales rose 15.5% to $2.46B and EPS of $0.35 beat $0.34, with operating margin up to 21.5%. But gross margin slipped 40 bps to 44.8%, 2026 capex was set at $310–330M (from $231M in 2025), and the shares fell about 4.5% pre-market to ~$49, from near a 52-week high. At 41× trailing earnings and above the $49.45 consensus target, FAST is fully valued. Over the next 10–30 days the stock trades in a quiet, range-bound regime that has historically been followed by gains; the October sales report in early November decides whether the dip is bought.
reports.headline: Fastenal's 15.5% growth quarter met a stock already priced above its targets, so the month turns on whether October daily sales keep accelerating

reports.dek: Q3 2026 sales hit a record €11.7B (+55% YoY) at a record 57.5% gross margin, and Q4 guidance of €14.2–15.2B implies the biggest quarter in the company's history. Management said planned capacity for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand, with some customers already asking about 2029–2030 orders. The Amsterdam line opened +2.2% and faded to +0.7%; the ADR was flat pre-market at ~$1,716 after falling 8% in seven sessions. Over the next 10–30 days ASML trades as a semiconductor-sector name (correlation 0.83 with the sector fund, beta 2.2 to the S&P 500), so the late-October chip-equipment and memory prints decide whether the re-rating starts.
reports.headline: ASML's demand now outruns its capacity into 2028, and an 8% pre-print pullback gives the semiconductor tape room to re-rate it inside the month

reports.dek: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.59 beat the $2.53 consensus and sales of $25.40B beat $25.28B, led by Innovative Medicine (+7.7%: Tremfya +68%, Darzalex +15%). Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose only $0.06 to $11.10, and MedTech grew just 2.5% with international sales +1.5%. A $5.5B talc charge cut GAAP EPS to $0.09. The shares were ~2.5% lower before the open at ~$257, after a 27% gain this year. Over the next 10–30 days J&J trades on a premium multiple (23.8× this year) with little market correlation; peer prints and orthopaedics separation news decide whether the pullback deepens.
reports.headline: J&J's beat-and-raise is a pharma story the market already owns, so a softer MedTech quarter sets up a month of consolidation, not a new leg higher

reports.dek: Five straight beats and a twice-raised outlook have not stopped a 32% slide, because the market is pricing leadership turnover, slowing bookings and AI disruption rather than the quarter. With no earnings print before mid-December and 99.5% of daily variance company-specific, the stock trades on news over the next 10–30 days: a fresh downgrade and a federal labour-program suspension weigh on it, while Adobe MAX on 10–12 November is the one dated event that could change the story.
reports.headline: Adobe keeps clearing the earnings bar, but the next month belongs to its headlines

reports.dek: Q3 2026 beat on revenue and EPS, but full-year core EPS growth guidance was cut to +1–2% from at least +4%, and the stock closed at a 52-week low of $123.73 after nine target cuts in two weeks. The next 10–30 days hinge on whether a cheap valuation holds against a regime backdrop that has rarely favoured PEP, with Coca-Cola and the late-October snack prints as the deciding catalysts.
reports.headline: PepsiCo's profit-guide cut was the reset the market had already priced, but at a 52-week low the month needs North American proof, not cheapness

reports.dek: Neogen beat Q1 FY27 revenue by 9% and nudged FY27 guidance up, trading 11% higher after hours, but with 97% of daily variance company-specific and the stock at its lowest Persistency reading of the year, the next 10–30 days hinge on the Investor Day and the HYCOAT warning-letter response, not the market.
reports.headline: Neogen's beat-and-raise bought a gap, not a trend — the month turns on whether it holds above $12

reports.dek: Penguin beat on Q4 sales and raised FY27 guidance 40%, but the stock had already risen 24% in 30 sessions with operating cash flow negative for the year, so the next 10–30 days test whether post-print target raises confirm demand before the July pattern of a sharp reversal repeats.
reports.headline: Penguin's raised guide is real, but a 24% run-up, three-times market beta and negative cash flow make the month a test of whether the gap holds

reports.dek: After the 1 October close Nike beat on EPS ($0.48 vs $0.43) but missed on revenue ($11.21B, -4%), guiding FY27 adjusted EPS to $1.15-1.35, about 22% below the $1.61 consensus. Shares fell 6.2% after hours to $32.96, a 13-year low, and the next 10-30 days hinge on whether consensus can reset lower into a stock at about 26x guided earnings, in the weakest regime backdrop of any name in this series.
reports.headline: Nike guided the year 22% below the Street and its dividend now exceeds its earnings; the month is about estimate cuts, not the bottom

reports.dek: Accenture rose 15.8% on 1 October, its best day on record, after a Q4 beat and $100M+ bookings hit a quarterly record. But the FY27 guide implies only about 0.5-4% organic growth, and the next 10-30 days hold the gain only if analyst upgrades and the October IT-services prints show AI adding to demand rather than deflating it.
reports.headline: Accenture's record rally repriced the AI fear, not the growth rate, so the month depends on whether peers confirm it

reports.dek: Jabil beat on every line and guided FY27 above consensus, but the stock fell 10% on a lighter margin guide and crowded AI-linked positioning, with the next 10–30 days testing whether that drop was overdone.
reports.headline: Jabil raised its outlook and lost a tenth of its value; the month tests whether that was positioning or a margin warning

reports.dek: Micron cleared every bar at seven times run-rate earnings, but the risk for the month is the cycle debate, not the numbers, with the stock trading at about 7× annualised guidance.
reports.headline: Micron cleared every bar at seven times run-rate earnings. The risk for the month is the cycle debate, not the numbers

reports.dek: A beat-and-raise lifted shares 13.4% on record yields and deposits, but with fuel unhedged and a soft Q4 guide, the next 10–30 days hinge on whether crude falls back below $100.
reports.headline: Carnival’s record quarter bought a floor, but oil decides whether the gap holds

reports.dek: A sixth straight beat-and-raise met an FTC antitrust review of the UniFirst deal, with no fixed timeline and the review itself the single event most likely to reprice the stock.
reports.headline: Cintas keeps beating and raising — the next 10–30 days hinge on an FTC clock, not the ledger

reports.dek: A beat on every line met a spike that gave back most of its gain, with the stock in a $56–$62.5 range ahead of the 10 November Investor Day.
reports.headline: Worthington beat the quarter and the market sold the spike — the next month is a range trade into Investor Day

reports.dek: A 15% earnings beat met an 11% pullback tied to sector, not the company, with the next 10–30 days trading on the alternative-manager complex and a ten-year yield near 5%.
reports.headline: Brookfield’s earnings keep compounding, but the next month belongs to its sector and the ten-year yield

reports.dek: A 50%-off-highs stock met a $763 million antitrust fine, with 94% of variance idiosyncratic and the next 10–30 days hinging on whether the regulatory chapter is closed.
reports.headline: Trip.com’s growth is intact. Its regulatory ceiling is not.

reports.dek: A margin turnaround with 69% revenue growth met missed delivery guidance and a fresh 52-week low, with the September delivery report due around 1 October deciding the next move.
reports.headline: NIO's turnaround is real; the delivery momentum that moves the next month has stalled

reports.dek: A beat and raised guide printed an all-time high before reversing to close up just 1.8%, with book-to-bill at 0.8 and no company catalyst until December.
reports.headline: SAIC beat, raised the guide, and spent the pop before lunch

reports.dek: A record quarter and the largest payout in years lands the shares at a 52-week high, with the next 10–30 days hinging on spot tanker rates against a scheduled dividend drop.
reports.headline: Frontline is minting cash at the top of the cycle — and the share price has already arrived.

reports.dek: A blowout beat on coffee pricing and tariff refunds pushed shares to a 52-week high and past the average analyst target, leaving a 99.9% idiosyncratic digestion trade.
reports.headline: Smucker's beat-and-raise is real — but the stock has already run past where Wall Street will follow.

reports.dek: Record premium customers and 16% revenue growth against a near-nil enterprise value, with the earnings catalyst spent and direction now hostage to China-internet sentiment.
reports.headline: Tuya trades for almost no enterprise value — but the next month rides China's tape, not the beat

reports.dek: A beat-and-raise quarter met with a 9.2% single-session drop on decelerating comps, leaving a 99.8% idiosyncratic name with no catalyst until November.
reports.headline: Walmart beat and raised — and the market sold the one line that missed

reports.dek: Cloud revenue accelerating 45% against a 75% profit drop, with a discounted $10.2bn Hong Kong share placement now the swing factor for the next month.
reports.headline: Cloud is compounding at 45%, but a $10bn discounted share sale owns the next month

reports.dek: A light revenue miss and a guide cut to the bottom of every range, offset by a cheap multiple and an 87.9% idiosyncratic setup ahead of the September FOMC.
reports.headline: Lowe's cleared a low bar and cut its guide — the next month is a valuation-and-macro trade, not a growth story

reports.dek: A best-in-class quarter and reaffirmed guidance met a flat tape, with no company catalyst until November and a premium multiple to defend.
reports.headline: Home Depot posted its strongest comp in years, and the tape shrugged

reports.dek: First earnings miss in eight quarters and a close below book value, with AI-cloud growth real but no catalyst before November.
reports.headline: Baidu's advertising decline outruns its AI, and the next month has no catalyst to close the gap

reports.dek: Record FY2026 EBITDA and the largest dividend in four years, against an FY2027 copper guide cut 11.7% — the next 10–30 days trade as a copper-price instrument.
reports.headline: BHP has never earned more from copper, and next year it has less of it to sell
